title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
next_steps: Samir to share the raw request/response logs for the 2026-04-01 incident by 2026-04-04
Aisha to run a targeted load test with 5k concurrent short requests and share results by 2026-04-06
Customer to validate retry/backoff settings in staging and confirm behavior by next sync (2026-04-09)
Samir to share updated retry/backoff recommended config and rate-limit settings
Schedule a brief benchmark run with dedicated capacity if rate-limit tuning doesn't resolve timeouts
action_items: Samir Patel: compile and send incident logs + request IDs for 2026-04-01 03:12 UTC outage — due 2026-04-04
Aisha Gomez: run targeted 5k concurrent requests test (short prompt, 16 token responses), attach trace and histogram — due 2026-04-06
Maya Chen: validate SRE-managed retry policy (exponential backoff, jitter) in staging and report anomalies — due 2026-04-09
Liam O'Connor: confirm current rate-limiter config and token bucket thresholds, share screenshots of nginx/ingress metrics — due 2026-04-05
transcript:
00:00 Samir: okay good morning everyone, uh thanks for joining. i'm Samir from Redwood. quick roll call, then we'll jump into the incident timeline and the test results. 00:10 Maya: hey Samir, Maya here. thanks. 00:15 Liam: Liam on the line. 00:18 Priya: Priya, SRE. 00:20 Diego: Diego product. 00:22 Aisha: Aisha, solutions eng at Redwood. Jordan's also on for notes. 00:30 Samir: cool. quick agenda — recap what happened late last night, discuss root causes (timeouts, 5xx cascades, rate limits), go over the new traces Aisha ran, and align next steps. 00:45 Maya: sounds good. quick context — we saw a spike of 5xx errors and timeouts around 03:12 UTC, about 15 minutes of elevated error rates. customer-facing API returned 504s intermittently. 00:58 Priya: yeah from our side we saw a sudden backlog on our ingress and a lot of retries from the app layer which then caused more load, so it looked like a retry amplification. 01:12 Liam: we also have a rate-limiter at the edge which started throttling some requests, not sure whether that was protective or made it worse. 01:22 Aisha: okay thanks. we looked at the Redwood side — initial signal is a combination of upstream slow tokenization on a few requests and our autoscaler reacting a bit late because the pod cold-starts with larger models. there were also a handful of 5xxs from a KV cache miss pattern — transcript sometimes reads it as K V cash — so apologies for the transcribe. 01:45 Samir: can you walk us through the trace Aisha? 01:50 Aisha: yeah i'll share screen — (note: link to traces/benchmark spreadsheet in chat). so at 03:10 we see a spike in p95 latency from 280ms to 1.8s, then timeouts at the client after 2s. a subset of requests hit a path that triggers a large kv-cache population which is expensive — that's the 5xx window. 02:18 Maya: when you say kv-cache population, do you mean loading the full prefix into memory? that was our hunch. 02:26 Aisha: yes — the model runtime tries to populate the KV cache for certain long-context prompts; when multiple concurrent requests do that it creates memory pressure and evicts other working sets which caused retries and 5xx errors. 02:38 Priya: we saw the app layer implement immediate retries with no backoff which amplified spikes. that's on us to change, but it would help if Redwood returned a clear retryable vs non-retryable header. 02:50 Samir: good point — we can add a header suggestion in the API. Aisha, any quick config changes we recommended? 02:58 Aisha: immediate recommendations: 1) enable short exponential backoff + jitter at client (we suggested example code in the playbook), 2) raise our model-level soft rate-limit threshold for the POC to reduce 429s at edge and allow graceful queueing, 3) enable KV caching warmup for common prompts in the staging Canary. 03:18 Liam: about the rate-limiter — if we raise it we risk letting too many cold-starts through and hitting the autoscaler; do you have metrics on cold-start latencies? 03:28 Aisha: yes, we captured cold-start histograms — cold-start p95 is ~1.2s with current image, we can push a smaller boot image to get that down to ~600ms for this POC. that was a config change we proposed in last week's doc. 03:44 Samir: and the 5xx class — were they internal server errors from the runtime or from our ingress? 03:50 Aisha: mostly runtime OOMs leading to 5xx, plus some gateway 502s when the runtime restarted. the runtime logs show spikes in memory usage correlated with the KV population events. 04:05 Priya: okay that matches our metrics. we'll throttle retries and add jitter client-side. 04:12 Maya: do you recommend we move to Dedicated for the POC to get more predictable throughput? 04:18 Jordan: note: customer asked about Dedicated. 04:20 Samir: we discussed Dedicated as an option — Dedicated gives reserved pool so cold-starts are less frequent and you get smoother p95s, but it costs more. for now we can try tuning retries, rate-limits, and a small runtime tweak. if the next run still shows instability, we'll spin up a small dedicated pool for a short benchmark. 04:40 Diego: for cost reasons we prefer tuning first. 04:44 Aisha: ok plan: i'll run a targeted synthetic test — 5k concurrent short requests (we'll mimic your production prompt mix) — to reproduce the retry amplification. i'll include both no-retry and exponential-backoff cases. 04:56 Samir: perfect. please also include a run with adjusted rate-limiter thresholds so we can compare. 05:02 Priya: on our side we'll patch the client retry policy today to add 200-800ms exponential backoff with jitter. 05:12 Liam: i'll export our ingress rate-limit config and send to Samir so you can recommend exact token-bucket sizes. 05:18 Samir: great — please attach screenshots. 05:21 Maya: also — can Redwood add a header like X-Redwood-Retryable: true/false? that will make it easier for our app to implement smarter logic. 05:30 Aisha: yes we can add guidance and a recommended header in the docs; we'll propose X-Redwood-Retryable with status values. 05:36 Samir: i'll also share the incident runbook and suggest a standard 5xx vs 429 handling section. 05:42 Maya: one more ask — can you share any known model variants that are less memory heavy? we thought quantized variants might help. 05:50 Aisha: yes model quantization helps; we listed compatible quantized variants in the model catalog spreadsheet (link in chat). recommend using q4_0 or q5_0 for lower mem footprint; we can test an as-needed fallback. 06:06 Priya: about logging — we need request IDs surfaced end-to-end. do you have a header for that? 06:12 Samir: we can return X-Redwood-Request-Id and echo it back in logs, we'll include that in the playbook. 06:20 Liam: for the targeted load tests, what's the exact prompt length we should mirror? Diego: our average request is small — 12 tokens out, 28 tokens in. 06:34 Aisha: okay we'll use short prompts with 16 token responses to force many quick calls. 06:38 Samir: timeline check — Aisha run by 2026-04-06, Samir shares logs by 2026-04-04, customer patches retry by 2026-04-05, follow-up sync next Thurs 2026-04-09. 06:52 Maya: agreed. 06:55 Diego: quick question — are there any SLA implications? if this keeps happening we'll need guaranteed throughput. 07:02 Samir: yes SLA is typically tied to Dedicated, but for the POC we can offer an elevated monitoring and an ops run if needed; we'll define scope in the follow-up email. 07:12 Priya: one last note — some of our 504s came from the downstream auth service timing out under retry pressure — not 100% Redwood's. we'll share correlation graphs. 07:25 Aisha: good to know. we'll correlate traces once we get their logs. 07:30 Jordan: captured notes and action items, will send meeting summary. 07:35 Samir: thanks everyone, appreciate the partnership. we'll follow up with logs and the playbook. 07:40 Maya: thanks, bye. 07:43 Liam: bye. 07:44 Aisha: thanks, have a good one.  

Notes: links mentioned in chat - traces: https://redwood.app/traces/abc123, benchmark spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-poc, model catalog snippet: https://redwood.app/models/qvariants. Attachments: none.
